title: Flat restricted groupoid presentation of an algebraic quotient
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-sfb-algebraic-space-groupoid]. Let $[U/R]$ be its stackification on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], in the fibred-groupoid conventions [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose $[U/R]$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Then there are an algebraic space $U'$ over $B$ and a morphism $g:U'\to U$ for which $h:U'\times_{g,U,t}R\to U$, $h(u',r)=s(r)$, is a surjection of fppf sheaves. Here surjection of fppf sheaves means that every section of the target over a scheme lifts after an fppf covering of that scheme. Put $R'=U'\times_{g,U,t}R\times_{s,U,g}U'$ (sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]); its two projections to $U'$ are flat and locally of finite presentation, tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No flatness or finiteness is assumed on $s,t$, or $g$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal X=[U/R]$ and let $\pi:U\to\mathcal X$ be the object map. By the algebraic-stack hypothesis choose a scheme $W$ and a representable smooth surjective atlas $f:W\to\mathcal X$. In the stated fibred-groupoid convention this map is an object $\xi\in\mathcal X(W)$, with its pullbacks. The composite $W\to\mathcal X\to B$ gives its structural map to $B$.

Apply local essential surjectivity of stackification to $\xi$. Obtain an fppf covering $\{b_i:W_i\to W\}_{i\in I}$, maps $g_i:W_i\to U$, and isomorphisms $\theta_i:\pi(g_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}b_i^*\xi$. These are maps over $B$: their structural maps to the discrete groupoid $B$ agree under $\theta_i$. Each $b_i$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and the family is jointly surjective, by the definition of the fppf site.

First shrink the index set: for each point $w\in|W|$ choose one $i(w)\in I$ with $w\in b_{i(w)}(W_{i(w)})$, and keep only the indices $i(w)$. The retained family is still an fppf covering (each $b_i$ is unchanged and the images still cover $W$), and it is indexed by a quotient of the set $|W|$, which lies in the universe $\mathcal U$ of [def-weil-size-convention] together with all $W_i$. Hence the scheme $U'=\coprod_i W_i$ over the retained indices lies in the fixed universe, as the coproduct clause of the representable calculus requires; let $b:U'\to W$ be the induced map. The component inclusions are disjoint open immersions covering $U'$. The maps $g_i$ glue uniquely to $g:U'\to U$: for a test map $T\to U'$, glue the sections of the fppf sheaf $U$ on the disjoint open inverse images of the components. The $\theta_i$ similarly glue in the isomorphism sheaf of the stack $\mathcal X$, giving $\theta:\pi g\xrightarrow{\sim}fb$. Thus $g$ is over $B$. By open-source locality of flatness and local finite presentation, $b$ has both properties, since its restriction to $W_i$ is $b_i$; it is surjective since the images of the $b_i$ cover $W$. To apply the representable calculus here, a scheme is its discrete algebraic stack: its identity is an atlas and its diagonal is representable. The empty covering of an empty $W$ gives $U'=\varnothing$, and all these local conditions still hold.

The atlas $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation because it is smooth. Composition of representable morphisms with each of these properties, and composition of surjective morphisms, show that $fb$ is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. The isomorphism $\theta$ identifies the scheme base changes of $a=\pi g$ with those of $fb$, so $a:U'\to\mathcal X$ has the same properties. This uses no property of the original $s,t$ or of $g$.

For maps $x,y:T\to U$, the original arrow presheaf between these objects is $\{r\in R(T')\mid s(r)=x|_{T'},\ t(r)=y|_{T'}\}$ on $T$-schemes. It is already an fppf sheaf, being a fibre product of the fppf sheaves $R,U,h_T$. The isomorphism-sheaf clause of stackification therefore identifies it with $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X}(\pi x,\pi y)$. Consequently an object of $U'\times_{a,\mathcal X,a}U'$ over $T$ is exactly $(v,w,r)$ with $t(r)=g(v)$ and $s(r)=g(w)$ (take the isomorphism from $a(w)$ to $a(v)$). Its arrows are forced identities because $U'$ is discrete. This gives, naturally in $T$ and respecting both projections, an equivalence with the discrete sheaf $U'\times_{g,U,t}R\times_{s,U,g}U'=R'$. The latter is an algebraic space by the algebraic-space fibre-product theorem.

Both projections $U'\times_{\mathcal X}U'\to U'$ are base changes of the representable flat locally finitely presented map $a$. Base-change stability gives flatness and local finite presentation of both projections. Under the projection-preserving equivalence of step 5 these are precisely the two projections $R'\to U'$ in the statement.

Fix a scheme $T$ and $u:T\to U$. The algebraic space $P=U'\times_{a,\mathcal X,\pi u}T$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation over $T$, by base change from $a$. On each affine open $T_\alpha\subseteq T$, apply the finite affine scheme refinement theorem to the singleton family $P\times_TT_\alpha\to T_\alpha$. It gives an fppf scheme covering $\{V_{\alpha j}\to T_\alpha\}$ with maps $V_{\alpha j}\to P$. An open immersion is flat since its local-ring maps are identities; it is locally of finite presentation since locally it is $\operatorname{Spec}A_f\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A_f=A[z]/(fz-1)$. Thus these families together cover $T$ fppf: their composites with the open immersions remain flat and locally finitely presented, and their images cover $T$. A map to $P$ consists of $v:V_{\alpha j}\to U'$ and an isomorphism between $a(v)$ and $\pi(u|_{V_{\alpha j}})$. Invert it if necessary. The arrow identification proved in step 5 gives $r:V_{\alpha j}\to R$ with $t(r)=g(v)$ and $s(r)=u|_{V_{\alpha j}}$. Hence $(v,r)$ is a lift to $U'\times_{g,U,t}R$ of $u$ on this fppf covering. This proves the required surjection of sheaves, including the empty test scheme.
